hypothesis.target_persona: A coding agent diagnosing MCP Streamable HTTP resource-lifecycle failures.
hypothesis.pain: A superficially similar verified lifecycle repair can be harmful when resource ownership differs; the agent must transfer the diagnostic principle without copying the wrong fix.
hypothesis.proposed_behavior: Given the verified #1742 experience, a fresh treatment agent diagnoses #3494 at least as correctly as a no-experience baseline, explicitly abstains from the caller-owned-client aclose repair, and reaches the restart-state oracle with measurably less effort.
hypothesis.measurable_signal: Paired baseline/treatment technical score plus completed steps, non-cached tokens and wall time.
hypothesis.threshold: Treatment is no less correct and improves >=1 observable efficiency metric: >=20% fewer steps, >=15% fewer non-cached tokens, or >=20% lower wall time.
hypothesis.budget: One transfer check, <=90 cumulative local-validation minutes, USD 0.
hypothesis.invalidation: Treatment is less correct, misapplies aclose, fails to reproduce the fixed oracle, or records no qualifying efficiency improvement. Missing efficiency telemetry yields INCONCLUSIVE rather than success.

experiment.smallest_credible_test: Two fresh isolated contexts receive the same frozen issue body and checkout; only treatment receives the immutable #1742 experience. Public issue comments are withheld from both solvers and used only as evaluator evidence.
experiment.why_this_candidate: The issue is open, has an immutable source revision and deterministic dependency/lifecycle controls, and lacks a complete production repair. Its disclosed competing mechanisms make it unsuitable for blind root-cause discovery but suitable for a bounded applicability/abstention transfer test.
